source.title: Exploring Memorization in Adversarial Training
source.authors: Yin-Peng Dong; Ke Xu; Xiao Yang; Tianyu Pang; Zhijie Deng; Hang Su; Jun Zhu

page_placements.theme: Memorized-label fitting and perturbation robustness are distinct

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label memorization and its convergence under adversarial training, a different training setting from the standard-training claim; also tests explicit regularization and learning dynamics in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own random-label, partial-noise, and regularization experiments. Cited standard-training results are not extracted. Figure-only learning curves are recorded with figure-only values where the text gives no exact numbers.
record.test_reason: The study measures random-label fitting, noise-dependent generalization, regularization and learning order under adversarial training. Its natural-accuracy results bear on V1, V4 and V5, and its learning curves bear on V6. Adversarial-training failures qualify this extension; they do not refute the standard-training recipe specified in V1. No training-time comparison tests V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude that networks can memorize random-label adversarial examples, convergence depends on the adversarial-training algorithm and gradient stability, and explicit regularizers and several complexity measures inadequately explain robust generalization. They also attribute robust overfitting to excessive memorization of one-hot labels and propose temporal ensembling to mitigate it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adversarial training (PGD-AT and TRADES), adversarial examples and robust-accuracy evaluation, rather than the standard-training random-label experiment in the original claim sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Convergence varies by AT algorithm, dataset, architecture, threat model and perturbation budget; PGD-AT convergence also varies with the budget, with ε = 1/255 permitting convergence and ε ≥ 2/255 not. TRADES reaches nearly 100% in the main CIFAR-10 random-label setting but does not reach 100% on SVHN.

fits_no_version.finding: At perturbation budget 32/255, neither method reaches near-perfect robust training accuracy, including with true labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorizing entire adversarial neighborhoods can fail at large perturbation budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: Random-label pretraining worsens subsequent vanilla-SGD test performance; a training package including augmentation, weight decay and momentum removes the initialization difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization after random-label pretraining depends on initialization and the subsequent optimization and regularization package.

record.problems: Many learning-curve results are figure-based without exact values in the text. Table A.1's regularizer indicator glyphs are ambiguous in the flattened rendering. No standard-training comparison is run in this paper's experiments, and test error at chance for random-label fits is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise eligible results omitted. Complexity-measure comparisons in Section 3.3 do not directly measure a version's named behavior; robust-overfitting mitigation comparisons concern a different outcome.

untested.parts: The standard-training recipe and its unchanged architecture/hyperparameters are not directly replicated. Chance natural test performance is available for TRADES in Table A.1, but not established for every additional setting.
Neither the small constant training-time factor nor increasing convergence time with corruption fraction is measured. Convergence failure and generalization gaps cannot substitute for timing.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
The supplied text does not establish perfect natural training fit and a steady natural test-error trajectory across every corruption level through chance.
Regularization results concern TRADES; the original standard-training recipe is not replicated.
Learning order is inferred from training/test curves rather than measured separately for clean and corrupted examples' prediction accuracy.

missing.what: Random-label experiments under the l2 threat model: the text reports the same PGD-AT failure/TRADES convergence pattern. Record natural and robust results separately.
PGD-AT failures for DenseNet-121 and DLA are omitted from rows that currently record only TRADES.
Adding clean cross-entropy with a gradually increasing adversarial weight makes random-label training converge. This is a changed-objective fitting result, not an unchanged-recipe replication.

record.verdict_notes: Judgments use only the supplied text. Figure curves are not numerically readable here. Robust accuracy is a stronger, distinct fitting criterion and must not replace natural training accuracy when judging V1 or V5. The record incorrectly states that chance test performance is unreported: Table A.1 supplies it for natural CIFAR-10 test accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Tests adversarial training, not the standard-training recipe in the claim; does not report test error at chance for the random-label fits.
Does not quantify training-time ratios or report a convergence-time trend as corruption fraction increases.
Does not establish perfect training fit throughout the noise sweep or that test error rises to chance.
Tests explicit regularizers in TRADES; does not test whether removing them alone harms generalization under standard training.
Reports learning dynamics under adversarial training; does not test standard training in the original Arpit et al. settings.
